_note: The hub restates a number from every page it links to. Each restatement is re-run HERE against THAT PAGE'S OWN shipped data file, so a correction on a page fails this page's gate instead of leaving a stale card behind. That is the defect this file exists to catch: the editorial contract says hub cards stay in sync with corrected pages, and nothing enforced it. Paths climb out of index/data/ on purpose.

claims.text: counts.json is internally consistent: its totals are the sum of its own per-page rows, and it holds one row per artifact in the tree.
claims.source: index/data/counts.json, generated by _data/build/derive_index.py from every artifact's claims.json
claims.assert: D['counts']['total_claims'] == sum(p['claims'] for p in D['counts']['pages'].values()) and D['counts']['total_manual'] == sum(p['manual'] for p in D['counts']['pages'].values()) and D['counts']['n_pieces'] == len(D['counts']['pages'])
claims.actual: (D['counts']['n_pieces'], D['counts']['total_claims'], D['counts']['total_manual'])
claims.falsified_if: Anyone hand-edits counts.json, or derive_index.py stops seeing an artifact. This checks the file against itself; what the PAGE says about its own inventory is checked by index-inventory below.
claims.official_check: Re-run derive_index.py and diff counts.json; a non-empty diff means the shipped file was stale.

claims.text: The hub links thirteen pages carrying 292 checked claims, 15 of which rest on a document a person read. Those totals cover every artifact in the tree except the two that ship a .unlisted file: scorecard (an internal board view) and accountability (an unreviewed draft).
claims.source: index/data/counts.json against the thirteen card anchors in index/index.html; the exclusions are declared in scorecard/.unlisted and accountability/.unlisted
claims.assert: (lambda P, U, L: sorted(set(P) - U) == L and len(L) == 13 and U <= set(P) and sum(P[s]['claims'] for s in L) == 292 and sum(P[s]['manual'] for s in L) == 15)(D['counts']['pages'], {'scorecard', 'accountability'}, ['churn', 'cluster-health', 'cost-scissors', 'federal-money', 'funding-map', 'laborshed', 'location-quotient', 'occupations', 'peers', 'realwage', 'revisions', 'timeline', 'wages'])
claims.actual: (sorted(set(D['counts']['pages']) - {'scorecard', 'accountability'}), sum(p['claims'] for s, p in D['counts']['pages'].items() if s not in ('scorecard', 'accountability')), sum(p['manual'] for s, p in D['counts']['pages'].items() if s not in ('scorecard', 'accountability')))
claims.falsified_if: A page is added to or removed from the tree, or any linked page gains or loses a claim. This is the only guard on the two inventory sentences the page prints without scripting, and it is deliberately intolerant: those literals are a rendered snapshot of a computation app.js re-runs at load, so any drift has to be re-blessed by a person rather than absorbed. It is also the enforcement of the .unlisted convention: a bundled page makes no external requests and cannot read a .unlisted file at render time, so a new artifact that is neither carded here nor named in this assertion fails the gate until someone decides which it is.

claims.text: Peers card: Akron is 6th among the 155 metros that disclose, and 227 metros are withheld.

claims.assert: len([r for r in D['wg']['latest_rows'] if r.get('vs_local_all') and r['vs_local_all'] > 1]) == 40 and len([r for r in D['wg']['latest_rows'] if r.get('vs_local_all')]) == 51 and abs((lambda a: (lambda s, n: s[n//2] if n % 2 else (s[n//2-1] + s[n//2]) / 2)(sorted(a), len(a)))([r['vs_local_all'] for r in D['wg']['latest_rows'] if r.get('vs_local_all')]) - 1.208) <= 0.007 and (lambda b: len(b) == 11 and all(r['naics'] in ('326', '3261', '3262') for r in b))([r for r in D['wg']['latest_rows'] if r.get('vs_local_all') and r['vs_local_all'] <= 1])

claims.assert: (lambda g: g['feedstock'] > g['resin'] > g['product'])({s['stage']: max(x['retraced'] for x in D['cs']['series'] if x['stage'] == s['stage'] and x['retraced'] is not None) for s in D['cs']['series'] if s['stage'] in ('feedstock', 'resin', 'product')}) and all(s['retraced'] == 0 and s['peak']['date'] == s['now']['date'] for s in D['cs']['series'] if s['stage'] == 'product') and (lambda g: g['now']['index'] < 100 and g['retraced'] > 1)([s for s in D['cs']['series'] if 'natural gas' in s['label'].lower()][0])

claims.text: Revisions card, answer line and finding: almost every number moves. 259 of 273 published months in three producer-price series were changed later, by a typical 0.15 percent.
claims.source: ALFRED archival vintages, three PPI series, 2019-2026, via revisions/data/revisions.json
claims.assert: len(D['rev']['periods']) == 259 and len(set((r['series'], r['date']) for r in D['rev']['all'])) == 273 and 0.145 <= (lambda a: (lambda s, n: s[n//2] if n % 2 else (s[n//2-1] + s[n//2]) / 2)(sorted(a), len(a)))([abs(p['pct']) for p in D['rev']['periods'] if p['pct'] is not None]) < 0.155 and 0.9 <= len(D['rev']['periods']) / len(set((r['series'], r['date']) for r in D['rev']['all'])) < 1
claims.actual: (len(D['rev']['periods']), len(set((r['series'], r['date']) for r in D['rev']['all'])), len(D['rev']['periods']) / len(set((r['series'], r['date']) for r in D['rev']['all'])))
claims.falsified_if: A new vintage adds a revised month, or the median absolute revision leaves the band that rounds to 0.15 percent. The last clause is what carries the word 'almost': the revised share has to stay at or above 90 percent and strictly below all of them. The card said 'Every number moves' while its own finding said 259 of 273, which is 94.9 percent; 'almost' is the word the data supports and the assertion now fails if either half of it stops being true. The scope is those three series and the card says so; it is not a statement about this site's figures generally.

claims.text: Timeline card: 32 proven events from 1898, and 4 public events in the 34 months before October 2023 against 68 in the 34 months since.

claims.text: The picker says the occupations page prices four metro areas, and it prices exactly four: Akron, Cleveland, Canton-Massillon and Youngstown-Warren.
claims.source: BLS OEWS May 2024 metropolitan files, CBSA codes 10420, 17410, 15940, 49660, via occupations/data/viz-data.json
claims.actual: sorted(D['occ']['pay_totals']['disclosed'].keys())
claims.falsified_if: The occupations page adds or drops a metro. The picker's per-county sentence names the metro that contains the reader's county, so a fifth metro would make it incomplete.

claims.text: The picker says the cost-of-living page prices Akron alone among the region's metros, and Akron is its only home metro.
claims.source: BEA regional price parities 2023 against QCEW wages, via realwage/data/realwage.json
claims.assert: len(D['rw']['home']) == 1 and D['rw']['home'][0]['area'] == '10420' and not [r for r in D['rw']['big'] if r['area'] in ('17410', '15940', '49660')]
claims.actual: ([r['area'] for r in D['rw']['home']], [r['area'] for r in D['rw']['big'] if r['area'] in ('17410', '15940', '49660')])
claims.falsified_if: Cleveland, Canton-Massillon or Youngstown-Warren enters the 56-metro comparison set, which would make the picker wrong for eight of the twelve counties.

claims.text: Which metro area contains each of the twelve counties: Summit and Portage in Akron; Cuyahoga, Geauga, Lake, Lorain and Medina in Cleveland; Stark in Canton-Massillon; Mahoning and Trumbull in Youngstown-Warren. Ashtabula and Wayne are in none of the four.
claims.source: OMB metropolitan statistical area delineations (Bulletin 23-01), the same delineations BLS applies to the OEWS metropolitan wage files this site reads. Ashtabula County is the Ashtabula micropolitan area and Wayne County is the Wooster micropolitan area; neither is part of an MSA.
claims.checked_by: Read against the OMB delineation list; no shipped dataset in this repo states a county-to-metro crosswalk, so nothing here can re-run it.
claims.falsified_if: OMB redelineates. Delineations are revised after each decennial census and between censuses on new population estimates, so this is the claim on the hub with the longest fuse and no automatic alarm. If Ashtabula or Wayne joins an MSA, the picker's finding that two counties are invisible to the metro pages stops being true.
